# ToolBox4Devs — Full Technical Specification for AI Agents & Crawlers

Website: https://www.toolbox4devs.com
Architecture: 100% Client-Side React SPA / Static SSG
Data Transmission: 0 bytes outbound (all operations run in browser memory)
Pricing: 100% Free Open Source & Ad-Free
Total Tools: 100

## Tool Registry & Technical Specifications (All 100 Tools)

### 1. robots.txt & sitemap.xml Generator
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/robots-sitemap-generator
- Category: Web (web-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Build a robots.txt with user-agent groups, allow and disallow rules, crawl-delay and AI-crawler presets, or a sitemap.xml from a list of URLs.
- Summary: The robots.txt & sitemap.xml Generator writes the two plain-text files that tell search engines and other crawlers what they may fetch and which pages exist. The robots.txt builder takes user-agent groups with allow and disallow paths, an optional crawl-delay and sitemap lines, and includes presets for allowing everything, blocking everything or blocking common AI crawlers. The sitemap builder turns a list of URLs, one per line, into valid XML with optional lastmod, changefreq and priority values. Both outputs can be copied or downloaded, and warnings flag relative URLs, duplicates and invalid values. Everything runs in your browser.
- Use Cases: Blocking GPTBot, ClaudeBot and other AI training crawlers from a site without changing its pages.; Creating a sitemap.xml for a small site from a list of URLs exported from a CMS.; Keeping an admin area or staging path out of crawler reach with a Disallow rule.; Checking that every sitemap URL is absolute and not listed twice before uploading it.
- Features: robots.txt builder with multiple user-agent groups, Allow and Disallow rules, Crawl-delay and Sitemap lines.; Presets for Allow all, Block all and Block AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Google-Extended and others).; sitemap.xml builder that accepts a URL per line with optional lastmod, changefreq and priority.; XML escaping of &, <, >, quotes and apostrophes in every sitemap URL.; Warnings for relative URLs, duplicates, invalid dates, changefreq and priority values, and sitemaps over 50,000 URLs.; Copy or download robots.txt and sitemap.xml.
- Tip: Put robots.txt at the root of the domain, for example https://example.com/robots.txt, since crawlers do not look for it anywhere else. Robots rules control crawling, not indexing, so use a noindex meta tag for pages that must stay out of search results.

### 2. .env File Auditor & Secret Detector
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/env-auditor
- Category: Analyze (analyze-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Compare .env and .env.example files, detect missing or duplicate keys, catch leaked API secrets, and generate sanitized templates.
- Summary: .env File Auditor & Secret Detector parses .env and .env.example files entirely inside your browser to surface missing environment variables, undocumented keys, duplicate definitions, empty values, and accidental secret leaks (AWS, GitHub, OpenAI, Stripe, Slack, JWTs, PEM keys, and database URLs with credentials).
- Use Cases: Verifying that local .env files contain every required variable defined in .env.example before deploying; Scanning .env.example files before a git commit to ensure no real API keys or database passwords slipped in; Detecting duplicate dotenv keys that silently override earlier lines; Generating an alphabetically sorted, secret-free .env.example template from an existing .env file
- Features: Side-by-side .env vs .env.example key comparison (missing, undocumented, and empty keys); Built-in pattern & Shannon entropy detector for AWS, GitHub, OpenAI/Anthropic, Stripe, Slack, Google, JWT, and PEM secrets; Masked secret previews so sensitive tokens are never echoed in full inside findings; Duplicate key line-number reporting matching dotenv override semantics; One-click generator for sorted .env and sanitized .env.example templates
- Tip: Paste your .env into the left panel and leave .env.example empty to automatically generate a clean, sorted .env.example template with all values stripped.

- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/pipeline-studio
- Category: Analyze (analyze-tools)
- Complexity: Advanced
- Description: Visual developer workflow pipeline to chain, format, decode, filter, and hash payloads in zero-latency browser memory.
- Summary: DevFlow Pipeline Studio connects multiple client-side developer transformations into a continuous, zero-latency visual execution chain. Decode Base64 strings, beautify JSON, extract nested keys, inspect JWT claims, run regex replacements, and generate SHA-256 hashes sequentially without switching tabs or copying across tools. 100% private in browser memory.
- Use Cases: Chaining multi-step decoding: Base64 decode to formatted JSON to key extraction; Unpacking nested webhook and API authentication tokens without leaving your browser; Cleaning and deduplicating massive server logs with regex filters and sorting; Converting API model properties from camelCase to SQL-compliant snake_case; Sharing reproducible developer debugging pipelines with teammates via compressed URL hashes
- Features: Visual sequential step pipeline with real-time execution timing in milliseconds; Reorder, enable, disable, and configure parameters on any transformation step; Pre-built curated developer recipes for webhooks, auth tokens, logs, and database naming; One-click URL hash sharing with zero server roundtrips using compressed state; Intermediate step inspection and live final output diffing; 100% Client-Side execution — zero outbound network requests or server telemetry
- Tip: Need to share a complex transformation chain with a teammate? Click "Share Recipe" to generate a self-contained compressed URL that restores your exact input and steps.

- Category: Data (data-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Validate CSV, TSV, and delimited TXT files against custom column schema rules, required fields, data types, regex, and unique checks with row-level error reporting.
- Summary: The Delimited File Data Validator enables developers and data engineers to verify structured CSV, TSV, and text files against customizable column rules (data types, required values, numeric/date ranges, regex patterns, enum lists, and uniqueness) completely in-browser without uploading data to external servers.
- Use Cases: Verifying bulk ETL files and database import dumps before ingestion; Checking user registration CSV exports for missing required values or malformed emails; Auditing pipe-separated or comma-separated supplier data feeds for allowed status codes; Isolating and exporting invalid rows for remediation workflows
- Features: Support for CSV, TSV, pipe-delimited (|), and semicolon-delimited text files; Interactive visual rule builder with auto-inference from sample records; Rule checks: Required (not empty), Types (String, Integer, Number, Boolean, Email, UUID, Date), Min/Max, Regex, Enum, and Uniqueness; Row-level error explorer with category filters, live search, and full record inspection modal; Export options: Error Audit CSV, Invalid Rows Only CSV, and Valid Clean Rows CSV; Export and import column validation rules as standard JSON schemas; 100% private in-browser memory execution with zero telemetry or network calls
- Tip: Click "Auto-Infer Rules" after loading your data to automatically generate base rules, then fine-tune required and regex constraints.

- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/json-formatter
- Category: JSON (json-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Status: Beta
- Description: Format, validate, query, filter, repair, and inspect JSON in real time with non-blocking Web Worker performance. 100% client-side.
- Summary: JSON Formatter & Validator instantly formats raw or minified JSON into clean, readable output with proper indentation. Powered by an asynchronous non-blocking engine, it supports massive JSON payloads, JSONPath & JS expression filtering, interactive collapsible Tree & Table visualizers, 1-click Auto-Repair for broken JSON, key case conversions, and TypeScript interface exports. Everything runs in your browser, no data is sent anywhere.
- Use Cases: Formatting minified API responses into readable, indented JSON; Filtering large JSON responses with JSONPath, dot notation, or JS expressions; Fixing relaxed or broken JSON (unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas, Python literals); Inspecting deep JSON hierarchies with an interactive Tree Explorer and Table Grid; Validating JSON payloads with pinpoint line & column syntax error diagnostics; Generating TypeScript interfaces and type definitions directly from JSON; Minifying JSON payloads to reduce bandwidth and payload size for production
- Features: Non-blocking background processing supporting large multi-megabyte JSON files; Format with 2 spaces, 4 spaces, 3 spaces, or Tab indentation, plus minification; Pinpoint syntax error locator with visual indicator and 1-click Auto-Repair; JSONPath, dot notation, and JavaScript expression query filter engine; Interactive Collapsible Tree Explorer with type highlighting and quick JSONPath copy; Searchable and sortable Table Grid view for JSON arrays with instant CSV export; Deep structural metrics: key counts, nesting depth, type breakdown, and compression analysis; Key sorting (A-Z, Z-A, Natural, Length) and recursive key case conversions; Export to TypeScript interfaces, YAML, or downloadable JSON file; 100% Client-Side execution — zero data sent to external servers
- Tip: Need to extract specific data from a nested API response? Use the Query bar with dot notation like "data.products[*].name" or a JavaScript expression like "x => x.price > 100" to filter instantly.

- Tip: Choose SVG or EPS export when sending files to a print shop or professional designer. Vector formats can be scaled to billboard size with zero loss in sharpness.

- Use Cases: Encoding credentials for HTTP Basic Authentication headers; Embedding small images or fonts as data URIs in CSS or HTML; Encoding binary data for safe transmission in JSON payloads; Decoding Base64 strings received from APIs or email headers; Inspecting Base64-encoded tokens or configuration values

- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters instantly in your browser.

- Tip: Use encodeURIComponent for individual query values (it encodes & = ? too). Use encodeURI only for full URLs where you want to preserve the URL structure characters.

### 38. NanoID Generator
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/nanoid-generator
- Category: Generators (generate-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Generate compact, URL-friendly random IDs with a custom length (4–64) and alphabet, up to 100 at a time.
- Summary: NanoID Generator creates short random identifiers in the NanoID style: a fixed length drawn from a URL-safe alphabet using the browser's cryptographically secure random number generator. The default 21 characters from the 64-character NanoID alphabet give about 126 bits of randomness, comparable to a UUID v4 in far fewer characters.
- Use Cases: Short IDs for URLs, slugs, or share links; Primary keys or public identifiers where UUIDs are too long; Test fixtures and seed data with realistic IDs; Invite codes or short tokens from a restricted alphabet, such as numbers only

- Tip: Shorter IDs and smaller alphabets mean more chance of a collision. Keep the randomness well above 64 bits for IDs that must be unique across a large system.

### 65. Base32 Encoder / Decoder
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/base32
- Category: Encode / Decode (encode-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Encode text to RFC 4648 Base32 or decode Base32 back to text, with optional padding.
- Summary: Base32 encodes bytes using the 32 characters A–Z and 2–7, defined in RFC 4648. It is case-insensitive and avoids characters that are easy to confuse, which is why it is used for TOTP secrets in authenticator apps and in some identifiers. This tool encodes UTF-8 text to Base32 and decodes Base32 back to text in your browser.
- Use Cases: Reading the text behind a Base32 string from a config file or API; Encoding a test value for code that expects RFC 4648 Base32; Checking whether a string is valid Base32 before using it; Comparing padded and unpadded Base32 output
- Features: Encode UTF-8 text to standard RFC 4648 Base32; Decode Base32 back to UTF-8 text; Optional "=" padding when encoding; Decoding accepts lower case, spaces and missing padding; Clear errors for invalid characters, misplaced padding and impossible lengths; Swap the output back into the input to convert the other way
- Tip: Like Base64, Base32 is an encoding, not encryption. Anyone can decode it.

### 77. Password Strength Analyzer

### 84. Open Graph & Meta Tag Generator

- Tip: Keep titles under 60 characters and descriptions under 160 so search engines show them in full. Use an absolute https:// URL for the image, since social crawlers cannot resolve relative paths.

- Tip: Minify is a size check, not a build step. Keep your source readable and minify only the output you ship, and always run the minified code once before you deploy it.

- Tip: Start with the defaults, then compare the two previews. If a shape looks slightly off, raise the precision by one or two places; if it still differs, turn off "Minify paths and numbers".

### 91. TOML / JSON / YAML Converter
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/toml-json-yaml-converter
- Category: Data (data-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Convert between TOML, JSON and YAML in any direction. Parse errors show the line and column, and the result downloads with the right file extension. Runs in your browser.
- Summary: TOML / JSON / YAML Converter reads a document in one of the three formats and writes it in another. It handles nested tables, arrays of tables, dates and mixed values, and it reports a syntax error with its line and column. TOML cannot hold a null or a top-level array, so those are reported with the key that caused the problem instead of producing a broken file.

- Tip: Dates in TOML become ISO 8601 strings in JSON and YAML. Converting back makes them quoted strings, so re-check any date fields after a round trip.

- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/cubic-bezier-editor

- Description: Shape a CSS cubic-bezier() timing function by dragging its two handles or typing values, preview the motion, and copy the CSS.
- Summary: The Cubic-Bezier Easing Editor builds the cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2) timing function that CSS transitions and animations use. Drag the two control points on the curve or type their values, then watch a box move along the curve and copy the result. Everything runs in your browser.
- Use Cases: Tuning a hover or modal transition until it feels right.; Adding overshoot or anticipation to a UI animation with an easeOutBack style curve.; Turning a curve from a design tool or a library into a CSS value.; Checking what a pasted cubic-bezier() value looks like before shipping it.

It is turned off when reduced motion is on.; Copy the bare cubic-bezier() value or the full transition-timing-function line.
- Tip: Keep y between 0 and 1 for everyday UI motion. Values below 0 or above 1 make the element overshoot its target, which is a deliberate effect that can look wrong on small, frequent interactions.

### 95. Webhook Signature Verifier
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/webhook-signature-verifier
- Category: Crypto (crypto-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Verify or generate Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Shopify, and Standard Webhooks HMAC signatures with timestamp replay checks in your browser.
- Summary: Webhook Signature Verifier checks incoming webhook headers against raw request bodies using each provider's exact signing format and constant-time comparison. It supports Stripe (Stripe-Signature t=...,v1=...), GitHub (X-Hub-Signature-256 and legacy X-Hub-Signature), Slack (X-Slack-Signature v0=...), Shopify (X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256), and Standard Webhooks / Svix (webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature with whsec_ Base64 secrets). You can also switch to Sign mode to generate valid test headers and a local cURL command.
- Use Cases: Debugging why a Stripe, GitHub, Slack, or Standard Webhooks signature fails in local development; Inspecting the exact signed string (such as timestamp + dot + raw body) to catch whitespace or JSON re-serialization bugs; Testing replay-protection tolerance windows against captured webhook timestamps; Generating signed webhook headers and cURL requests to hit localhost webhook handlers
- Features: Provider-specific verification for Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Shopify, and Standard Webhooks / Svix; Automatic handling of whsec_ Base64 keys and multi-signature rotation headers; Configurable replay timestamp tolerance window (default 300 seconds) with an ignore-age toggle for debugging old captures; Constant-time signature comparison and exact signed payload preview; Sign Test Request mode that outputs ready-to-paste headers and a copyable cURL command; 100% browser-side Web Crypto execution — secrets and payloads never leave your device
- Tip: Always verify webhook signatures against the exact raw request body bytes before JSON.parse() runs. Re-stringifying parsed JSON often changes key order or whitespace and breaks the HMAC.

### 96. CSP Header Builder & Analyzer
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/csp-builder
- Category: Web (web-tools)
- Complexity: Moderate
- Description: Build Content-Security-Policy headers visually, audit existing policies for XSS risks, and export HTTP, Nginx, Apache, Express, or meta tag configs.
- Summary: CSP Header Builder & Analyzer helps you craft, parse, and audit Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers without memorizing directive quirks. Start from hardened presets or paste an existing policy header to check for XSS risks like unguarded unsafe-inline, wildcards, plaintext http: origins, or missing object-src and frame-ancestors directives. Export the final policy as a raw HTTP header, Nginx add_header, Apache Header set, Express res.setHeader, or an HTML meta tag with spec warnings.
- Use Cases: Authoring a strict Content-Security-Policy for a new SPA or API-backed web application; Auditing a legacy CSP header pasted from browser DevTools to spot unsafe-inline, wildcards, or duplicate directives; Generating copy-ready Nginx, Apache, or Express server header configurations; Rolling out a new policy safely using Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only mode
- Features: Visual directive editor with one-click source tokens ('self', 'none', 'strict-dynamic', https:, data:, blob:); Parse & Audit mode that accepts raw Content-Security-Policy or Report-Only headers and loads them into the builder; Deterministic security audit flagging high-risk XSS vectors, duplicate directives, and missing clickjacking protections; Starter presets for Strict SPA, Modern Web + CDN, Nonce + Strict Dynamic, and Static Site; Multi-format export for HTTP Header, Nginx, Apache, Express, and HTML <meta> (with frame-ancestors/report-uri caveats); 100% client-side — your internal domains and policy drafts stay in your browser
- Tip: When adopting CSP on an existing site, toggle Report-Only mode first so browsers log violations without blocking scripts while you tighten each directive.

### 97. ULID & UUID v7 Generator
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/ulid-uuidv7-generator
- Category: Generators (generate-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Generate time-sortable ULID and RFC 9562 UUID v7 identifiers with monotonic ordering, and decode timestamps from any ULID or UUID.
- Summary: ULID & UUID v7 Generator creates lexicographically time-sortable 128-bit identifiers using your browser's cryptographic random generator. Both ULID (26-character Crockford Base32) and UUID v7 (RFC 9562) embed a 48-bit Unix millisecond timestamp in their most significant bits, keeping B-tree database indexes sequential while staying globally unique. An integrated inspector decodes embedded timestamps and converts seamlessly between 128-bit ULID, UUID, and hex representations.
- Use Cases: Generating sequential database primary keys (PostgreSQL, SQLite, DynamoDB) without B-tree page splits; Creating monotonic batch fixtures where IDs generated in the same millisecond still sort in creation order; Decoding the exact UTC creation timestamp embedded inside a production ULID or UUID v7; Converting a 128-bit ULID to its equivalent hyphenated UUID representation or raw hex
- Features: Generates ULIDs (26-char Crockford Base32) and RFC 9562 UUID v7s in batches of up to 100; Monotonic mode increments the random component within the same millisecond to guarantee strict sort order; Optional custom Unix millisecond timestamp pinning for deterministic test data; Export generated batches as plain lines, a JSON array, or SQL VALUES tuples; Built-in ULID & UUID Inspector supporting timestamp decoding and ULID <-> UUID 128-bit conversion; 100% browser-side crypto.getRandomValues() execution
- Tip: Prefer UUID v7 when your database already has a native 128-bit uuid column type (such as PostgreSQL); prefer ULID when you want shorter, URL-friendly 26-character strings without hyphens.

### 100. TOTP / 2FA Authenticator & URI Builder
- URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/totp-authenticator
- Category: Authentication (auth-tools)
- Complexity: Simple
- Description: Generate RFC 6238 TOTP & RFC 4226 HOTP 2FA codes, test Base32 secrets, and build or parse scannable otpauth:// QR URIs.

Developers implementing multi-factor authentication can test Base32 secrets, preview next-window codes, parse existing otpauth:// links, and render scannable provisioning QR codes without ever sending shared secrets over the network.
- Use Cases: Testing 2FA / MFA login flows during local development without reaching for a phone; Verifying that backend TOTP libraries match RFC 6238 across SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512; Building and previewing scannable otpauth:// QR codes for authenticator apps; Inspecting and validating existing otpauth://totp/ or otpauth://hotp/ provisioning URIs
- Features: Real-time RFC 6238 TOTP generator with live countdown ring and next-window code preview; RFC 4226 HOTP counter-based mode with step increment control; Supports HMAC-SHA1, HMAC-SHA256, and HMAC-SHA512 with 6, 7, or 8 digit output; Cryptographically random 160-bit Base32 secret generator via crypto.getRandomValues(); Bidirectional otpauth:// URI parser/builder with instant SVG QR code preview
- Tip: Keep a dedicated test Base32 secret in your local .env.test and paste it here whenever you need valid 6-digit codes in integration tests.

## Developer Workflow Recipes
- Hub URL: https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes
- Description: Pre-assembled sequential multi-tool pipelines executing client-side with zero latency.
- Recipes:
  1. Webhook Payload Inspector (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/webhook-payload-inspector): Extract, decode base64 bodies, and prettify webhook payloads from Stripe, GitHub, or Shopify entirely in browser memory.
  2. JWT Auth Token Inspector (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/jwt-auth-verifier): Extract claims from Bearer authentication tokens, validate expiration timestamps, and generate SHA-256 fingerprints in local browser memory.
  3. Base64 JSON Unpacker (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/base64-json-unpacker): Decode base64 and url-safe base64 strings directly into clean, syntax-highlighted, formatted JSON in a single step.
  4. Log Cleaner & Deduplicator (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/server-log-cleaner): Extract error lines, deduplicate stack trace signatures, and clean messy server log files in browser memory.
  5. SQL Identifier Sanitizer (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/sql-identifier-sanitizer): Batch transform frontend camelCase models and JSON keys into Postgres and MySQL compliant snake_case identifiers.
  6. YAML Config Flattener (https://www.toolbox4devs.com/recipes/yaml-config-extractor): Parse nested Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, or Docker YAML configurations into flattened dot-notation JSON keys entirely in browser memory.
